title: Feed weekly summary style chooser
content:
Feed's weekly TL;DR tool just moved from a single generated draft into a compare-and-choose editor, which is a much better fit for how these summaries are actually written.

What changed:

  • Six generated options at once: the weekly summary editor now shows all six summary styles side by side instead of one dropdown preview at a time.
  • Direct comparison workflow: each option shows its label, purpose, and rendered preview so the strongest version can be chosen in context.
  • One-click handoff into editing: Use This Style drops the selected generated version into the editable summary box, where it can still be refined before saving.
  • Style registry preserved in shared files: the available summary types are now exposed from styles.json, keeping the system easier to tune later.

The point of this pass was editorial control. Weekly summaries stay hand-selected and hand-written, but the generation step is now much better at helping compare voice, compression, and emphasis before publishing.
